newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - FLYERS BEAT PENGUINS IN LAST GAME FOR LEMIEUX.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - FLYERS BEAT PENGUINS IN LAST GAME FOR LEMIEUX.

text.p: The Philadelphia Flyers advanced to the Eastern Conference semifinals for the third straight season and ended Mario Lemieux's remarkable career with a 5-3 victory Saturday over the Pittsburgh Penguins.
Rod Brind'Amour tied a playoff record with a pair of shorthanded goals in a 54-second span of the second period for Philadelphia, which won the best-of-seven series 4-1.
The Flyers will play the New York Rangers or Buffalo Sabres in the second round.
Lemieux, who has confirmed he would retire after Pittsburgh's run in this season's playoffs, had a goal and an assist in his final game.
The 31-year-old Lemieux was last in line for the ceremonial handshake and received a prolonged standing ovation from the CoreStates Centre crowd after his name was flashed on the scoreboard.
Lemieux hugged Philadelphia's Eric Lindros, one of the players expected to carry his legacy into hockey's next century, before waving to the crowd and skating off to the locker room.
"I'm glad we won but in a sense it's a sad day for the NHL with Mario retiring," said Lindros.
Jaromir Jagr, Pittsburgh's star right winger, said: "It's a sad day for all of us. Mario made me a better player. I almost can't believe he won't play anymore."
At New Jersey, Martin Brodeur recorded his fifth career playoff shutout and the New Jersey Devils advanced to the Eastern Conference semifinals with a 4-0 victory over the Montreal Canadiens.
Four different players scored for the Devils, who won the best-of-seven series 4-1 and will play the Ottawa Senators or New York Rangers in the next round.
Brodeur, who led the league with 10 shutouts during the regular season, was rarely tested in making 24 saves.

Theodore came off the bench to stop 56 shots in Thursday's triple-overtime win that helped Montreal avoid just the third four-game playoff sweep in team history. But not even he could prevent the Canadiens from going down in the first round for the third time in as many post-season appearances.
Kevin Dean, inserted in the lineup after coach Jacques Lemaire moved defenceman Scott Niedermayer to right wing, scored the only goal Brodeur needed with 2:28 to go in the first period.
Said Brodeur, "I had it easy, there were only two or three real scoring chances. We played very well and shut them down almost completely until late in the game when the outcome was not in doubt."
Montreal right winger Stephane Richer said: "They shut us down completely, especially in the first period. I said it before and I say it now, I think New Jersey will win the Stanley Cup."
